sections.rationale: Establishes the foundational pipeline from typed task graphs through geometric realization to singularity extraction and back, including three concrete routes (graph hypersurface, quiver variety, discrete Morse) and catastrophe-theoretic enrichment of agent task graphs.

Motivates and defines hyperbolic geometry as the natural host for agent task graphs, covering negative-curvature hierarchy encoding, group-action quotients for monodromy loops, boundary memory, and the concrete hyperbolic graph extrusion with node regions and edge corridors.

sections.section_name: Whitney Stratification of Agent State Space
sections.rationale: Defines how the agent state and control space is decomposed into behavioral regimes via Whitney stratification, with agent state components (memory, evidence, confidence, budget) determining strata, catastrophe-theoretic mode switches at discriminant boundaries, and the partition map assigning states to strata.

sections.section_name: Group Symmetry, Quotient Compression, and Singularity Strata
sections.rationale: Describes how group-symmetry quotients collapse equivalent agent tasks into singular strata and how the partition map classifies agent states by dominant action, stabilizer type, constraint signs, and rank signatures.

sections.section_name: Energy Function and Partition Function over Strata
sections.rationale: Defines the statistical energy function and partition function that weight behavioral strata by cost, uncertainty, and conflict, and shows how softmax and energy-based ML models learn the stratified geometry from agent traces.

sections.section_name: Grammar, Compiler, and Typed Field Pipeline
sections.rationale: Describes the formal grammar-to-stratified-geometry bridge: a procedure grammar is compiled through ML scoring into typed quantitative fields and evaluated deterministically, yielding a four-layer system (grammar, ML scorer, state machine, distribution) that maps agent procedures to geometric objects.

sections.section_name: Scaling, Full Component Assembly, and Efficiency
sections.rationale: Characterizes the scaling behavior of the network (objects, relations, depth), assembles the complete thirteen-component hyperbolic agent object A_hyp, and summarizes efficiency gains from typed grammar, graph constraints, hyperbolic hierarchy, group quotient attention, IDF weighting, and structure-before-model allocation.

sections.section_name: Reservoir Computing Readout and Expert Validation
sections.rationale: Frames the full architecture as a reservoir-computing readout (frozen LLM plus structured typed-graph-geometric layer), clarifies the role of hyperbolic geometry as phase space, and reports the ML expert panel consensus on the system's promise and required validation steps.
